hero.title: Shareholder meetings and board meetings, run digitally
hero.description: You prepare the notice with the agenda, the items to vote on and the documents, review it and send it. Sttok certifies delivery and shows who has received it and who has not. Each shareholder logs in to their portal, sees the agenda and the documents, and appoints a proxy or votes if voting is open. Everything counts towards the quorum straight away.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about meetings and boards

items.q: Can I call the general meeting from Sttok?
items.a: Yes. The notice is prepared with its agenda and documents, sent to each shareholder, and the proof of delivery is kept.
The shareholder chooses a proxy and instructions and signs the proxy. The meeting shows at all times how much capital has been delegated.
Yes. It calculates the quorum for first and second call with confirmed attendance, proxies and early votes.

items.q: Does Sttok provide the video call?
items.a: No. The company uses its usual tool. Sttok handles attendance, voting and the minutes.

items.q: Does it also cover the board of directors?
items.a: Yes. It calls board meetings with their agenda and documents, keeps the minutes, certifies resolutions and records officers with their terms. It also handles attorneys and board committees.

items.q: Does it work for companies in Latin America?
items.a: The platform adapts to each country's terminology: shareholder ledger, general shareholders' meeting, board of directors. Compliance with each country's regulations is assessed case by case.

setup.title: A meeting in Sttok, from the notice to the signed minutes
setup.lede: Board meetings follow the same path, with their agenda, their documents and a calendar invitation for each director.

steps.title: Prepare and review the notice
steps.text: The agenda, the items to vote on with the majority each needs, and the documents are prepared digitally. Everything is reviewed before sending, and a test email can be sent.

steps.title: Certified delivery
steps.text: Sttok sends the notice to each shareholder and their representatives, certifies delivery and shows who has received it and who has not, so reminders go out in time.

steps.title: Proxies and attendance
steps.text: From delivery onwards, each shareholder appoints a proxy from their portal: they choose a representative, say how to vote and sign on screen. Proxies are recorded automatically and count towards the quorum straight away. On the day, attendance is marked.

steps.title: Voting
steps.text: During the meeting, the secretary opens and closes voting on each item. Shareholders vote from their portal, also on their phone, or the secretary records the votes of those in the room.

steps.title: Minutes and certificate
steps.text: At the end, Sttok drafts the minutes and the certificate of resolutions with attendance and the result of each vote. They are reviewed and sent for signature with DocuSign.

steps.title: Everything is filed
steps.text: The signed minutes and certificate are kept in the meeting documents, and the log records every delivery, proxy, vote and signature with its date and time.

situations.title: Common situations in meetings and boards

rows.situation: The annual general meeting has to be called
rows.action: The notice is prepared with the agenda and documents, sent to each shareholder and kept with its proof of delivery.
Signed proxies and early votes are collected, and the quorum is calculated with what is already committed.
Live voting is run item by item. The company provides the video call with its own tool.

rows.situation: A resolution needs an enhanced majority
rows.action: When the item is created, the majority needed to pass it is set, including an enhanced one above half plus one. Sttok applies it when voting closes.
Dates are booked, the agenda starts from the previous meeting and the notice goes out with a calendar invitation.

rows.situation: The minute book has to be legalised
rows.action: One book is kept per governing body and financial year, with its legalisation recorded.
